cover.kicker: Study for the Ministry of Energy of Kestria (fictional)
cover.title: Unlocking energy efficiency: potential, levers and barriers
cover.sub: Final report of the national energy efficiency study.

exec.title: Kestria can abate {tot40} of CO2e a year by 2040 and most of it costs little or nothing

rows.p: Industry holds {ind40} of the potential in 2040; buildings {bld40}, transport {trn40} and power {pwr40}. More than half of it costs less than the energy it saves over the life of the measure.
Four measures pay back on their own: smart controls, efficient motors, waste heat recovery and logistics efficiency. The rest need support, standards or both before firms and households will act.

rows.h: Cost is not the main barrier
rows.p: Split incentives, skills and grid capacity block more potential than upfront cost does. Interviews with firms point to the same four barriers in every sector.
Standards for buildings, an industrial efficiency fund and a fleet programme cover nine of the eleven measures. Each package has one lead ministry and a review date.

bullets: Potential grows from {tot30} in 2030 to {tot40b} in 2040 as stock turns over.
